newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg warns of downswings ahead.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg warns of downswings ahead.

text.p: Danish brewing giant Carlsberg on Monday announced slightly better than expected annual results but warned that growing competition and fluctuating global economies could mean periodic downturns in coming years.

"Constantly growing competition combined with the group's commitment to retain its position among the foremost players in the international brewing industry may, also in coming years, lead to declining financial results for brief periods," it said.
A commentary issued with Carlsberg's 1995/96 results added that it nevertheless expected a general pattern of steady growth.

The brewer, part-owner of Britain's Carlsberg-Tetley, on Monday announced pre-tax profits up more than 10 percent to 1.57 billion crowns ($270.1 million) in 1995/96, from 1.42 billion the year before, on turnover of 18 billion crowns, compared to 17 billion.
It logged a rise in earnings per 20-crown share to 16.63 from 15.69 but proposed leaving the dividend unchanged at 17 percent.
Its share slipped by just over two percent, to 373 crowns at 1230 GMT from Friday's closing 382 crowns. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650 ($ = 5.811 Danish Crowns)
